    Glossary

    The terms used across the dashboard.
    Balls per boundary
    Legal balls faced divided by fours plus sixes. Lower means more attacking; under 6.5 was never beaten this season.
    Dot ball
    A legal delivery with no runs off the bat and no wide or no-ball. Byes and leg-byes count as dots for the bowler.
    Economy
    Runs conceded per six legal balls; wides and no-balls count against the bowler, byes and leg-byes don't.
    Strike rate
    Runs per 100 balls faced (wides not counted as balls faced).
    Powerplay / middle / death
    Overs 1–6, 7–17 and 18–25.
    Runs per innings (rpi)
    Total runs divided by innings, not outs — so not a batting average.
    Impact / composite score
    Our own simple ranking: 1 point per run, 20 per wicket, half a point per dot ball bowled. Catches excluded (only season totals exist).
    Win probability
    An estimate from this season's scoring only: projected total against the target or the season par. A guide to where a match tipped, not a forecast.
    Appearance
    Being in the CricClubs match-day squad (up to 12), whether or not the player batted or bowled.

    Pressure batting

    Each batter's strike rate in the 10 balls after a wicket falls, and in the last five overs of a chase. Batters with 20+ pressure balls.

    Singles as a share of balls faced, and the longest run of consecutive dots. Batters with 60+ balls.

    Batting against the situation

    In chases: each batter's strike rate when the team was behind the required rate against when it was ahead. Batters with 20+ chase balls.

    Finishers

    Who was at the crease when the innings ended, how often, and what they scored in the last three overs.

    Dot-ball pressure and wickets

    How often a wicket falls within three balls of a run of four or more dots — for our batters (pressure we absorb) and our bowlers (pressure we create).
